stemMd: Two objects at different temperatures are placed in thermal contact in an insulated enclosure. In which direction does heat initially flow spontaneously?

options.label: A
options.textMd: From the heavier object to the lighter object

options.label: B
options.textMd: From the hotter object to the colder object

options.label: C
options.textMd: From the colder object to the hotter object

options.label: D
options.textMd: From the smaller-volume object to the larger

options.label: E
options.textMd: No heat can flow in an insulated enclosure.

explanationMd: Heat flows spontaneously down a temperature difference. Insulation prevents external exchange but permits internal transfer between the hotter and colder bodies.

distractorRationale.e: Insulation blocks exchange with outside, not between the objects.
distractorRationale.c: That would not be the spontaneous direction in this setup.
distractorRationale.a: Mass alone does not determine heat-flow direction.
distractorRationale.d: Volume does not determine the direction.
